quote: Evening, all things thou bringest / Which dawn spread apart from each other; / The lamb and the kid thou bringest, / Thou bringest the boy to his mother.
source: Sappho, fragment 104a, the Hesperus fragment, in Wharton’s Sappho (trans. J. A. Symonds, 1883)

evidence.where: The Bibelot, Volume I, Number V, which reprints Wharton's page of selected renderings for this fragment, read this run: the quatrain stands verbatim and is credited to J. A. Symonds, 1883, beside Edwin Arnold's 1869 version and Byron's imitation
evidence.edition: Henry Thornton Wharton, Sappho: Memoir, Text, Selected Renderings and a Literal Translation; Symonds rendering of 1883
evidence.locator: fragment 95 in Wharton's numbering, 104a in Lobel and Page

reason: The four lines match the Symonds rendering exactly, with the semicolon after each other and the line-head capitals kept. The source no longer claims a Wharton edition and page that were not opened; the Symonds credit is what the witness carries. Sappho has no other line in the year.
